facts.statement: The genus Planicoxa was described by DiCroce and Carpenter in 2001.
Planicoxa lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
Fossils of Planicoxa were discovered in Utah, United States.
facts.quote: Its fossils were discovered in Utah, United States.

facts.statement: The type species Planicoxa venenica was first described by Tony DiCroce and Kenneth Carpenter in 2001.
facts.quote: The type species for the genus is Planicoxa venenica, first described by Tony DiCroce and Kenneth Carpenter in 2001.

facts.statement: The fossils of the type species were found in the Poison Strip Sandstone Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation in Grand County, Utah.
facts.quote: Its discovery was made in the Poison Strip Sandstone Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation in Grand County, Utah, United States.

facts.statement: The species name venenica is Latin for "poison," referencing the Poison Strip Sandstone Member where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: venenica, the specific name, is Latin for "poison" in reference to the Poison Strip Sandstone Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation where the discovery was made.

facts.statement: The known fossils include a well-preserved ilium, femurs, tibias, vertebrae, and other material.
facts.quote: The taxon is represented by a well-preserved ilium, femora, tibiae, and vertebrae, as well as other material.

facts.statement: While the femurs are typical for ornithopods, the ilium features a short, horizontal postacetabular process that functions as an antitrochanter.
facts.quote: The femora are standard for ornithopods, but the ilium has a short, horizontal postacetabular process that is functionally an antitrochanter.

facts.statement: Planicoxa venenica is estimated to have reached a length of 4.5 meters and weighed 450 kilograms.
facts.quote: The species is estimated to have reached 4.5 m and weighed 450 kg.

facts.statement: A second species, P. depressa, was established by Carpenter and Wilson in 2008 for material originally named Camptosaurus depressus by Charles Gilmore in 1909.
facts.quote: A second species, P. depressa, was created by Carpenter and Wilson (2008) for material previously named Camptosaurus depressus by Charles Gilmore in 1909.

facts.statement: The material for P. depressa was collected from the Lakota Formation near Hot Springs, South Dakota.
facts.quote: That material was collected from the Lakota Formation near the town of Hot Springs, South Dakota.

facts.statement: In 2011, P. depressa was reassigned to its own genus, Osmakasaurus.
facts.quote: In 2011, it was assigned to its own genus, Osmakasaurus.

facts.statement: Planicoxa belongs to the infraorder Ornithopoda.
Planicoxa is classified within the unranked family Iguanodontia.
Planicoxa lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately 120 million years ago during the Aptian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 120 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The species was discovered in the Poison Strip Sandstone Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation in Grand County, Utah, USA.
facts.quote: Su descubrimiento fue hecho en la arenisca Poison Strip miembro de la Formación Cedar Mountain en el condado de Grand, Utah, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: The taxon is represented by a well-preserved ilium, femur, tibias, vertebrae, and other material.
facts.quote: Este nuevo taxón es representado por un ilion, un fémur, tibias, y vértebras bien preservadas, así como otro material.

facts.statement: The remains belong to at least two individuals, with an estimated length of 6 meters, a height of 2 meters, and a calculated weight of 900 kilograms.
facts.quote: Los restos pertenecen al menos a dos individuos, con un largo aproximado de 6 metros, un alto de 2, con un peso calculado en 900 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The time range for Planicoxa is estimated from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
